scope: Existing 224 us AFE/Q diagnostic only. No simulator launched and no source, deck, model or waveform modified. Only this README and summary written.

waveform.hash_note: Hash copied from the existing independent periodicity audit; this review did not claim a new before/after waveform hash.
waveform.reader: numpy.loadtxt(usecols=...) retained only these 22 of 112 columns; no SPICE execution.
waveform.method: Window boundaries linearly interpolated; all saved interior samples retained. Time mean: sum(dt*(y0+y1)/2)/T. AC RMS: remove that window mean, then sqrt(sum(dt*(z0*z0+z0*z1+z1*z1)/3)/T). RMS includes deterministic switching ripple and residual drift, not random noise or ENOB.

last_cycle.timing_caveat: Crossing times are linearly interpolated saved-wave measurements, not an assertion of picosecond accuracy or timestep convergence.
last_cycle.interpretation: Large ripple repeats at input chopper transitions; a later stable cycle mean does not remove these spikes.

bias_q_diff: Exact source text equality after replacing cap_nmos_03v3 -> audit_q_nmos and cap_pmos_03v3 -> audit_q_pmos. No other bias-circuit text change.

findings.finding: VCM is the midpoint of two nominal 100 kohm poly resistors, not an ideal voltage source or active buffer. Source explicitly calls for off-chip VCM-pad decoupling; the current deck has no explicit external VCM capacitor. This does not mean total VCM capacitance is zero.

EP and EN are ideal voltage sources between each electrode and the VCM node. They force electrode common mode to equal VCM and can return input-switch charging current to VCM; there is no independent electrode impedance model.

Physical input TGs, W20/W40 um with m=256, precede the large Cin. Input chopper edges correlate with the VCM extrema. Charge injection/feedthrough is a strong candidate, but port-current contributions were not saved.

VCM also connects to CMFB reference gates, disabled OFFDAC group parking switches, disabled CPF trim paths, and 16 output-to-VCM resistors per side. OFEN=0 parks about 61.38 pF nominal MIM per half (122.76 pF total) at VCM. These plus parasitics mean VCM is not an unloaded divider.
Older ADC and end-to-end benches explicitly used 100 nF at VCM; end-to-end bench also used 100 ohm per electrode leg. Neither establishes the actual board specification for this diagnostic.

Nominal unloaded-divider Rth is about 50 kohm; 100 nF gives about 5 ms. This is only a divider-alone estimate, not the full loaded circuit settling constant. Output resistors, active circuit paths, startup and initial charge change it. Adding a capacitor cannot reuse the 224 us window as automatic settling proof.

There is no direct Q MOSCAP on VCM. Q replacements occur in bias filters (21 instances) and VCLK decoupling (10 instances). Q can affect VCM indirectly through bias and clock edges. VCLK drops to 2.805756 V in the fixed window, making the clock path relevant, but this is not proof of a Q-model artifact.

proposed_next_diagnostics_not_executed: Complete the planned matched zero-input control with the exact same original topology, timing and numerical settings. It separates stimulus-dependent behavior from offset/switching effects; it does not by itself identify the VCM current path.

In an explicitly separate diagnostic, separate the electrode voltage-source return from VCM while preserving its commanded common-mode waveform (e.g. controlled source to ground). Save source/port currents to isolate return-path loading. Treat the change as a bench experiment, not a real electrode model or acceptance run.

Obtain actual board VCM capacitance, ESR/ESL, source impedances and startup requirements. If unknown, use clearly labelled sensitivity cases only; do not pick 100 nF as the specification. Bound runtime and declare appropriate transient/ripple criteria before running.

Save currents through EP/EN, VCM divider, output-load returns, CMFB reference branch, OFFDAC parking and any external capacitor; integrate per-edge charge and check KCL. Existing voltage-only waves cannot uniquely separate them.

Separate VCLK/bias formulation and timestep sensitivities in bounded diagnostic cases while preserving original PDK files. A C(V)/Q(V) law comparison alone does not prove equal numerical conditioning or ripple convergence.

Report reference VCM, output common mode and differential ripple separately; retain all switching outliers. Do not equate deterministic ripple RMS or the fixed mean-periodicity pass with low-noise/ENOB acceptance.
limitations: No unique causal attribution without current or controlled comparison data.
No new simulation, PDK qualification, low-noise performance, PVT/mismatch or full ADC/DWA validation.
Existing fixed 8-cycle periodicity pass remains valid only for its original declared scope and thresholds.
